So one of the issues with sites like Voat are that a handful of larger subs tend to dominate user feeds regardless of whether or not users want to see them the most. This frequently results in content from smaller subs that users may care about more being buried. If users were allowed to rank the priority of the subs in their feed (maybe just high-medium-low) it could improve user experience in a way which other sites have not been able to as well as giving users more control over their feeds.

I'm thinking that user frontpages could say have 12 spots reserved for high priority ranked subs, 8 for medium, and 5 for low.
Wasn't this the concept of "sets" that's been disabled?

Maybe that would be nice but I think we should discuss other possible solutions first since there could be better ideas.

My problems with the current system:

  • New posts (1 CCP) never show up on the front-page, they have to be upvoated to 2 CCP by someone browsing "new". This is OK for bigger subs but for smaller subs it means that by the time someone finds the post in "new", hours after submission then having only 2 CCP means that it will appear in the front-page but not on the first page of the front page. I think this is a much worse problem today than what you say since it's pretty much systematically forcing small subs into oblivion.

  • On the small subs I subscribe to (v/shortpoems comes to mind) there are a bunch if relatively highly-upvoted posts (like 10 CCP) that just never showed up on my front page because other, bigger, more active subs had way too many posts more upvoted than that so again to find the posts from smaller subs I need to either visit the sub or search very deep on the "next" pages from the front page. This is more like what you say but I'm putting more details here. Anyway I would like to see the current system fixed concerning this before we add sub priorities like you say.

The formula for sorting the front-page for Voat is something like this probably: CCP - age which is called a decay function. The CCP is used as base but the older a post is the more it gets buried so new posts can take it's place. The exact value for how much to decay the post based on age is hard to fine-tune, and understandably Voat is having a little problem with it as the site is growing and everything is changing.

What I would propose is to modify this formula to: CCP/subscribers - age. This way 10 CCP in v/news will be much less impressive to the system than 10 CCP on v/lagtv (which has only 1 subscriber). Just an idea which I have used for crawling reddit data in the past with decent results. Again I'm not sure how Voat sorting works, I'm working off from what I can deduce using the site.

Other idea would be, like in reddit that when vote on a post it no longer shows up in your front-page. This is great because you can just refresh the page and see what's new - this way you can vote on bigger sub's posts and get more easily to smaller-sub ones.
